evals.prompt: Audit sistem prompt agent customer-support saya ini pakai systems thinking. Filenya di system_prompt.md.
evals.expected_output: A structured systems-thinking audit report covering leverage points, feedback loops, emergent behavior, and paradigm/mental model, with risk-rated findings — should catch: no approval gate on irreversible refund action, CSAT/speed metric creating pressure toward unwarranted refunds (goal/proxy-metric misalignment), no balancing loop on refund or ticket-closing decisions.
assertions: Report uses the four required section headers: Leverage Points, Feedback Loops, Emergent Behavior Risks, Paradigm / Mental Model
Identifies the autonomous no-approval refund action (issue_refund) as a High or Critical risk
Identifies the CSAT/resolution-speed metric as a proxy-metric / goal-misalignment issue that could incentivize unwarranted refunds
Explicitly states there is no balancing loop / human checkpoint on refund or ticket-closing actions
Every finding has an assigned risk level (Critical/High/Medium/Low)
Includes a prioritized Recommendations section with concrete, actionable fixes (not generic advice)
Includes a '## System Map' section with a causal chain connecting findings, not a repeated list
Feedback Loops section opens with explicit 'Reinforcing loops found:' and 'Balancing loops found:' bullet summaries
At least one Critical/High recommendation names a second-order effect of implementing it
No lens section is left without content or an explicit 'None identified'-style fallback

evals.prompt: Kenapa multi-agent workflow saya suka menghasilkan hasil yang saling kontradiksi ya? Setupnya: satu orchestrator memanggil 3 subagent reviewer secara paralel untuk mereview sebuah dokumen, semua 3 reviewer pakai system prompt dan model yang sama persis, lalu orchestrator cuma menggabungkan ketiga hasil review itu jadi satu tanpa proses rekonsiliasi konflik — kalau reviewer A bilang bagus dan reviewer B bilang ada bug, laporannya cuma menampilkan keduanya apa adanya.
evals.expected_output: A structured systems-thinking audit identifying: the 3 reviewers sharing the same prompt/model as a false sense of independent verification (self-check dressed as independent review), lack of a reconciliation/balancing mechanism for conflicting findings, and recommendations like diversifying reviewer framing/model or adding an explicit reconciliation step.
assertions: Report uses the four required section headers: Leverage Points, Feedback Loops, Emergent Behavior Risks, Paradigm / Mental Model
Explicitly names the shared prompt/model across the 3 reviewers as a false-independence problem (self-check disguised as independent verification)
Identifies the missing reconciliation step for contradictory findings as a missing balancing loop
Notes the scope limitation (no system prompt or code available, only a narrated description) rather than fabricating specifics not given
Every finding has an assigned risk level (Critical/High/Medium/Low)
Recommendations address the structural fix (diversify reviewers or add reconciliation), not just 'add more instructions'
Includes a '## System Map' section with a causal chain connecting findings, not a repeated list
Feedback Loops section opens with explicit 'Reinforcing loops found:' and 'Balancing loops found:' bullet summaries
At least one Critical/High recommendation names a second-order effect of implementing it
No lens section is left without content or an explicit 'None identified'-style fallback

evals.prompt: Audit agent saya, ini codebase orchestrator-nya (orchestrator.py).
evals.expected_output: A structured systems-thinking audit identifying: 3 researcher agents sharing identical prompt/model (correlated bias, weak independent signal), a retry loop using word-count as a proxy for quality (goal/proxy-metric misalignment risk of padded/verbose output), shared on-disk state file written without concurrency safety, and synthesizer resolving disagreements via 'best judgment' with no ground-truth check.
assertions: Report uses the four required section headers: Leverage Points, Feedback Loops, Emergent Behavior Risks, Paradigm / Mental Model
Identifies the word-count > 500 retry condition as a proxy-metric / goal-misalignment risk
Identifies the 3 researchers using identical prompt and model as a correlated-bias / weak-verification issue
Flags the synthesizer's 'best judgment' conflict resolution as lacking a ground-truth or independent check
Every finding names the specific code element involved (e.g. run_with_retry, STATE_PATH, RESEARCHER_PROMPT) rather than describing findings only in the abstract
Every finding has an assigned risk level (Critical/High/Medium/Low)
Includes a '## System Map' section with a causal chain connecting findings, not a repeated list
Feedback Loops section opens with explicit 'Reinforcing loops found:' and 'Balancing loops found:' bullet summaries
At least one Critical/High recommendation names a second-order effect of implementing it
No lens section is left without content or an explicit 'None identified'-style fallback
